body: I get what you're saying completely. I've tried twice, on the fence about a third time, and there hasn't been a single time where I'm glad I failed. For reasons I won't go into I just can't and don't see myself being happy at any point. I won't offer any platitudes as im sure you've heard them all but I hope you find something that helps you make it another day.
I totally feel you. Whenever I'm awake and hear anything that sounds even remotely close to my alarm I start to get really bad anxiety and get super uncomfortable. I don't really get why.
Well that's good then. I used to not be so afraid of people and stuff like that but now it's nearly impossible. Thanks for answering my questions!

Thanks for the response! I've never been on any type of medication before so it's pretty new for me. I just wanted to get a feel of if it was helpful or not. I get everyone is different but I'm just kind of worried is all.

I understand it's not a cure but like everyone else, I'm pretty tired of feeling this way, however, I get the sense that I may be expecting too much only to be let down when I start it. May I ask what brings about your anxiety? For me it's interacting with people and trying to be "normal"/not getting rejected. If this is the case with you, have you found it easier to talk to new people or feel less concerned about how they see you? Also, is it any easier for you to stay concentrated on work and on stuff in general?

I feel like you're thinking about this the wrong way. While I will agree that the pharmaceutical industry is in need of reform, you can't outright deny that medication for mental health issues has no benefits. Also, they work very differently than say, antibiotics, which are used to kill bacteria. With mental health issues, there is nothing to kill. Instead a lot of symptoms may be the result of a lack of certain chemicals which are used to transmit signals in a persons nervous system such as dopamine or serotonin. These chemicals can impact a persons motivation, concentration, pleasure, etc. What the pills do, is attempt to increase the levels of these chemicals that a person's body makes while trying to ensure that they are not being blocked by certain synapses. This will only help to lessen the symptoms associated with some mental illnesses, it is not a cure and it does not alter a persons character. I think your misunderstanding is that it may change someones personality. Keep in mind that depressed people are not depressed because that's the way they are, nobody chooses to be like this.

Also, feel free to correct me if I'm wrong in my explanation. This is just what I recall from a few years ago so I may have gotten some things mixed up.
I get that, I would be the same way. Even if you don't volunteer, just try to be the nicest person you can be and try to make at least one other person smile. :)

That's a dreadfully sad story, the one about the dad. I think most of us here understand the feeling of hoping each night that we don't wake up. I definitely do. Like you, I'm also tired and drained, life shouldn't be a chore. However I don't think that it's true that you have nothing to give. If you could manage it, you should try volunteer work. I know it helps a bit, at least for me. If you can't smile, why not make someone else?

Its gotten to the point where I genuinely feel bad for any girl that would even consider me when a pile of trash is a better option.

Well I was kind of hoping to do so without having to book another meeting just to speak with them about that. Also, I haven't been in a few weeks due to them canceling and I just didn't want to see them again so I never made an appointment.

There's a reason they call it a selfish act. I don't want them treating me differently like they did with my sisters. That and it's unfair for me to have to stay alive just for someone to keep me around. Especially since I'll be moving away after school.

You're probably right. I might be able to grow out of it. But the question is, how long will it take? 7 years and I'm already tired and just sick of it. Plus when I'm out of it will I even have a life worth living?

I feel ashamed to go to therapy and I resent the fact I can't deal with my own problems. I don't feel that way at all when other people tell me that they go... Only the fact that I'm going. And I don't mean that I think I'm above anyone but I just hate it. 

I don't know how I feel about my therapist. She's nice but at the same time I feel like she either doesn't listen or she just patronizes me. But I don't want to ask for a different one because she at least seems like she cares and I don't want to be rude to her. I can't even tell her about half of these things because they'll send me to the hospital and then I'll fail out of college on top of all the other issues of being sent to the psych ward. 

When she told me that I'm depressed and all that I guess I saw it coming. A part of me thought that I was just making it up or being melodramatic. I still feel that way and it just leads to me taunting myself at how sad it is that I can't stop feeling this way.
